question: Should autoreview make the proposed Claude subscription and Bedrock models, effort levels, refusal fallback, and provider-authentication isolation the persistent default contract for existing users?
rationale: The branch selects new reviewer and fallback policy and changes authentication and configuration precedence; automated tests cannot determine the intended compatibility contract or whether fallback model invocation should be implicit.

options.title: Keep defaults opt-in
options.body: Preserve current-main behavior and expose the new model, effort, fallback, profile, and Bedrock choices through explicit flags or environment settings.

options.title: Adopt new defaults
options.body: Make the proposed behavior standard, with documented upgrade semantics and live proof for every supported authentication path.

options.title: Split hardening from policy
options.body: Land credential and process isolation separately while deferring model and fallback defaults to a smaller sponsored change.

recommendation.title: Keep defaults opt-in
recommendation.body: Preserve current-main behavior and expose the new model, effort, fallback, profile, and Bedrock choices through explicit flags or environment settings.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main history shows this person introduced and repeatedly maintained the autoreview and panel behavior whose contract would change.
